definitions.explanation: A sense of confidence in one's own abilities, achievements, or qualities. Carries a positive connotation of justified pride rather than arrogance.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{仕事|しごと}に{自負|じふ}がある。
examples.english: I take pride in my work.

examples.japanese: {日本一|にほんいち}だと{自負|じふ}している。
examples.english: I'm confident that we are the best in Japan.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{経験|けいけん}があるという{自負|じふ}が{彼|かれ}を{支|ささ}えていた。
examples.english: The pride in his many years of experience sustained him.

notes:
Expresses a confident belief in one's own worth or ability. Unlike {自慢|じまん} (boasting), {自負|じふ} implies a quieter, more internalized sense of confidence. The verb form {自負|じふ}する means "to pride oneself on" or "to be confident that."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自負|じふ}する: to pride oneself on; to be confident
- {自負|じふ}がある: to have pride/confidence
- {自負|じふ}{心|しん}: self-esteem; pride

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自慢|じまん}: boasting; pride — more outwardly expressed, can be positive or negative
- {誇|ほこ}り: pride; honor — broader, can be pride in others or one's group
- {自信|じしん}: self-confidence — focuses on believing in one's ability to succeed
